candidate_relation.name: CONSTANT_AUGMENTED_SIGNED_LITERAL_SUBSTITUTION_TRANSPORT
candidate_relation.map: Each target variable may map to a signed source literal or to Boolean constant 0/1; negated target literals use the complemented image.
candidate_relation.verification: Each target clause image must evaluate TRUE, be tautological, or contain a source clause as a subset. A supplied certificate is polynomially checkable.

theorem.claim: For every target CNF A and every satisfiable source CNF B, a constant-augmented substitution transport B -> A exists iff A is satisfiable.
theorem.forward: If A is satisfiable, let alpha be any satisfying assignment of A and map every target variable v to the constant alpha(v). Every target clause then evaluates TRUE, independently of B.
theorem.reverse: If a valid transport exists and B is satisfiable, take any source model. The soundness theorem for the transport induces a target model, hence A is satisfiable.
theorem.equivalence: SAT(A) iff EXISTS_CONSTANT_AUGMENTED_TRANSPORT(B -> A), for every fixed satisfiable B.
theorem.complexity_effect: Existence/discovery of this transport class is NP-complete already with a fixed satisfiable source, because it contains ordinary SAT witness search as the all-constant subcase.
theorem.R44BW_instance: The R44BW no-literal-substitution pair is trivially transportable after constants are allowed because both siblings are SAT; a satisfying assignment of the retained target is itself a constant transport certificate.

effect_on_TRUMP.positive: Constants make the relation strictly more expressive and can destroy the finite R44BW no-literal-substitution obstruction.
effect_on_TRUMP.barrier: The extra expressivity does not create a polynomial L3 mechanism; unrestricted discovery is exactly SAT-hard because the certificate may simply encode a satisfying assignment.
effect_on_TRUMP.next_frontier: Seek a broader relation whose supplied certificate is polynomially verifiable but whose discovery does not contain arbitrary SAT witness search as a trivial special case.
